items.title: Avoiding the "Bad Training, Faster" Trap in the Age of Al
items.summary: Al can build a course in minutes. That's the problem.L&D teams are being told to use Al for everything and ship more content, faster. But most training already fails to change what people do on the job. Making it faster doesn't fix that. It just gets us to forgettable sooner.In this session, you'll see why so much Al-made training gets ignored. It isn't wrong. It's generic, and people tune out generic. Through side-by-side examples of the same content built two ways, you'll see what Al can't supply on its own. Then you'll get a simple way to give it the context that makes people pay attention, remember, and act.What we'll cover:The real bottleneck isn't speedAl fixed production. But production was never our problem. Attention and follow-through are. More content, faster, just means more noise fighting for the same few minutes of focus.Why Al content slides right offDefault Al output is accurate and easy to ignore. We'll watch one prompt produce two very different results and name what the weak one is missing: personal stakes, real context, and a reason to care.Give Al what only you knowBefore you prompt, answer four questions. Who is this for? What do they struggle with? What should change? How should it feel? Your answers to turn a generic phishing course into one built for a real team: billing clerks who get fake invoices at month-end, when everyone is rushed and nobody wants to be the one who held up a payment.
